reasoning: In the KOKKOS style the guards are on Nij, the number of (i,j) pairs in the ENTIRE atom block: compute() sets 'nij = NeighborCount(numij, rcutsq, gi1, ni);' (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:272) for a block of up to atomBlockSize=2048 atoms and passes it down through blockatom_energyforce(ei, fij, ni, nij) into blockatom_base_descriptors(bd, Ni, Nij), where the tests read 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))' (line 1421), '(nl4 > 0) && (Nij>2)' (line 1443), '(nl33>0) && (Nij>3)' (line 1452), '(nl34>0) && (Nij>4)' (line 1460), '(nl44>0) && (Nij>5)' (line 1468); blockatom_energyforce() repeats the same Nij tests for crossdesc_reduction and the force coefficients (lines 1641-1668).  The reference EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1195-1320) applies the identical thresholds to Nj, the neighbor count of the ONE atom being processed: 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', '(nl23>0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl33>0) && (Nj>3)', '(nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl34>0) && (Nj>4)', '(nl44>0) && (Nj>5)', and this is the routine PairPOD::compute() actually calls (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:214).  Consequence: for an atom with <=5 neighbors sitting in a block that has many pairs overall, KOKKOS evaluates three-/four-body and cross descriptors that the CPU sets to zero (bd1 is zeroed first, eapod.cpp:1207), and those descriptors are not zero for small Nj (e.g. d33 = d3*d3 from a single-neighbor sumU).  Energies and forces for undercoordinated atoms (dimers, gas-phase monomers, adatoms, small clusters) therefore differ between pod and pod/kk.  Conversely, the KOKKOS guard can also switch off the terms for a whole block that happens to have few pairs.  Forces use the same Nij guards, so the KOKKOS result is at least self-consistent, but it does not reproduce the CPU model.
fix: Make the guards per-atom rather than per-block: the block already has the per-atom pair counts in numij (numij(i+1)-numij(i) is atom i's neighbor count).  Either pass that count into the kernels and mask each atom's contribution (write zeros for atoms below the threshold), or drop the Nij thresholds and instead zero the whole bd/cb block (see F0383) and multiply each atom's three-/four-body/cross terms by a per-atom mask derived from numij.
